findings.description: CON-SUP-103 permits a task to start at the limit and defines a late start as later than the limit. The requirement detects a fault when the task has not started within the limit, leaving the equality boundary ambiguous.
findings.requested_change: Define the detection condition so a start exactly at the configured limit is accepted and a later start is a fault.

findings.description: CON-SUP-103 permits execution up to the limit but calls execution longer than the limit an overrun detected at expiry. The requirement does not resolve how execution ending exactly at expiry is distinguished from an overrun.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the equality boundary and detection instant with the source owner, then specify an objectively distinguishable condition.

findings.description: The requirement refers to an allowed range but neither it nor CON-SUP-115 defines complete allowed values for configuration fields. CON-SUP-115 names a timing limit longer than the period, a zero period and an unknown task as out-of-range cases.
findings.requested_change: Specify or reference the allowed configuration values and identify the cases that must cause code 9; record unresolved limits as open points.

findings.description: The unconditional refresh at every control-cycle end conflicts with SYS-SUP-013, which prohibits refresh when a fault has been detected since the previous refresh, and with STK-SUP-005's healthy-task condition.
findings.requested_change: Qualify the scheduled refresh with the applicable health and fault conditions so the obligations are consistent.

findings.description: STK-SUP-005 permits watchdog servicing only while every supervised task is healthy. No detected fault since the previous refresh does not establish that every task is healthy, and may allow refresh after an earlier fault.
findings.requested_change: Specify the source-supported health condition for both watchdog refreshes and its relationship to detected and latched faults.

findings.description: The requirement says to verify program-code integrity but provides no reference value or method for deciding whether the check succeeds. OP-SYS-001 records that these are undecided.
findings.requested_change: After the source decision, specify or reference the integrity check and its acceptance criterion.

findings.description: The condition that the start-up program-code integrity check fails cannot be determined without the check method and reference value identified as undecided in OP-SYS-001.
findings.requested_change: After the source decision, reference an objectively defined failure criterion for the check.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 supplies the CRC-32 polynomial but not the other parameters needed to reproduce its value, such as initialization, reflection and final transformation. A matching stored value alone does not define a unique test.
findings.requested_change: Reference a complete CRC definition or record the missing parameters as an open point for a source decision.

findings.description: The requirement calls for a run-time code check but does not define how a segment is checked or judged intact. OP-SYS-001 records the missing method and reference value.
findings.requested_change: After the source decision, specify or reference the run-time integrity check and its acceptance criterion.

findings.description: The condition that a run-time segment check fails cannot be determined without the check method and reference value identified as undecided in OP-SYS-001.
findings.requested_change: After the source decision, reference an objectively defined failure criterion for the segment check.

findings.description: The unconditional reset request after entering the safe state also applies to a start-up configuration fault, whereas SYS-SUP-009 and CON-SUP-115 require that fault to latch the safe state. It also lacks an exception for the latch required by SYS-SUP-026.
findings.requested_change: Specify the reset behavior and its exceptions for latched safe-state conditions consistently with the source decisions.

findings.description: OP-SYS-002 records that CON-SUP-110 does not resolve when the latch applies relative to the third fault and third reset. The requirement repeats that ambiguity, preventing a consistent test sequence.
findings.requested_change: After the source decision, specify the exact event at which the latch takes effect.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 requires the latch and fault history to survive software and watchdog resets but not power loss. The requirement states only reset retention and omits the power-loss behavior.
findings.requested_change: Specify the source-required behavior of the latch and fault history on power loss.

findings.description: The unconditional high status after start-up checks pass conflicts with SYS-SUP-027, which requires the status signal to remain low while the safe state is latched. A software or watchdog reset need not clear that latch under CON-SUP-110.
findings.requested_change: Qualify the operational status transition to respect a retained safe-state latch and other applicable fault conditions.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 defines entities as task names, CODE or CONFIG, but does not determine the entity for watchdog-reset fault code 8. OP-SYS-003 records the missing decision, so a complete report for that fault cannot be judged.
findings.requested_change: After the source decision, specify the permitted entity for a watchdog-reset report.

findings.description: The response contains <state>, but neither the requirement nor CON-SUP-113 defines its permitted values or their meanings. OP-SYS-005 records the unresolved state vocabulary.
findings.requested_change: After the source decision, specify or reference the status values and their meanings.

findings.description: The instruction to return the last 8 fault reports does not define the response when fewer than eight reports exist, including immediately after a power-on with no retained history.
findings.requested_change: Specify the response for fewer than eight available reports, or record the missing behavior as an open point.

findings.description: CON-SUP-116 requires fault-injection hooks to exist only in test builds. The requirement requires them in test builds but does not prohibit their presence in other builds.
findings.requested_change: State the source-required restriction that the fault-injection hooks exist only in test builds.

findings.description: The trigger requires detection when execution has not completed at the limit, while the same statement exempts completion at that instant. CON-SUP-103 specifies both an overrun longer than the limit and detection at expiry; OP-SYS-008 records the unresolved boundary and detection instant.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the expiry and simultaneous-completion semantics with the source owner, then state one consistent trigger and detection time.

findings.description: After a reset that preserves a latched safe state, a fault-free control cycle can satisfy the stated refresh condition, but SYS-SUP-043 prohibits refreshing while the safe state is latched. CON-SUP-110 requires the latch to survive software and watchdog resets.
findings.requested_change: Align the scheduled refresh condition with the latch and fault conditions in SYS-SUP-043.

findings.description: The statement restricts when the independent watchdog may be refreshed but never requires a refresh while healthy. An implementation that never refreshes it would satisfy this statement, although STK-SUP-005 calls for servicing the watchdogs and CON-SUP-106 specifies a 100 ms timeout.
findings.requested_change: Specify the required independent-watchdog servicing behavior and timing under the permitted healthy conditions, using an agreed source or recorded derivation.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 supplies the CRC polynomial, but OP-SYS-010 identifies missing parameters and data-range details. The stated test cannot uniquely determine the expected CRC or whether the verification is correct.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and reference a complete CRC definition and the covered data and stored-value representation.

findings.description: The reset obligation is triggered only after the fault report has been transmitted. If transmission has not completed within 20 ms of entering the safe state, the statement imposes no reset request by the deadline, whereas CON-SUP-110 requires the report followed by a reset request within that interval.
findings.requested_change: Define the required reset sequence and deadline from safe-state entry without making the deadline conditional on a potentially late transmission; resolve any infeasible timing with the source owner.

findings.description: Retention of the safe-state latch and retention of the fault history across resets are independently judgeable: either can be lost while the other is retained. CON-SUP-110 requires both.
findings.requested_change: Split latch retention and fault-history retention into independently verifiable obligations.

findings.description: After the checks pass and the stated conditions hold, the requirement to drive the status signal high has no response time. CON-SUP-109 identifies high as operational, but the item gives no measurable point by which that indication must appear.
findings.requested_change: Define a source-supported response time or precise event for asserting the operational status, or record the missing decision as an open point.

findings.description: The trigger applies to every GET FAULTS request and requires eight reports even when fewer exist; SYS-SUP-044 explicitly establishes an empty history after power restoration. OP-SYS-011 records that CON-SUP-113 does not define the response for fewer than eight retained reports.
findings.requested_change: Limit the eight-report obligation to the applicable retained-history condition and specify the response for zero to seven reports once the source owner decides it.

findings.description: CON-SUP-116 says fault-injection hooks exist only in test builds. The statement requires hooks in test builds but does not prohibit them in other builds, so it does not express that source constraint.
findings.requested_change: Add an independently verifiable obligation that the fault-injection hooks exist only in test builds.

findings.description: Clearing the safe-state latch and emptying fault history after restored power are independently judgeable outcomes: one can succeed while the other fails. Both are addressed by CON-SUP-110.
findings.requested_change: Split the post-power-loss latch and fault-history outcomes into independently verifiable obligations.

findings.description: The requirement says to drive the status signal high when the stated conditions hold, but gives no deadline or precise event for doing so. A test cannot determine how long a low signal remains acceptable. OP-SYS-012 records that the inputs do not provide this timing.
findings.requested_change: Obtain a source-owner decision and state a measurable response bound or precise event for driving the status signal high.

findings.description: The requirement does not define how program-code integrity is checked or the reference value used to judge it. CON-SUP-107 supplies neither; OP-SYS-001 records the missing decision.
findings.requested_change: Define the check method and reference value once the source owner decides them.

findings.description: Failure of the start-up program-code integrity check cannot be determined without the method and reference value missing from CON-SUP-107 and recorded in OP-SYS-001.
findings.requested_change: Define the failure criterion once the check method and reference value are decided.

findings.description: The requirement specifies the segment size and frequency but not how a segment is checked or judged intact. OP-SYS-001 records the missing method and reference value.
findings.requested_change: Define the segment check and acceptance criterion once the source owner decides them.

findings.description: Failure of a run-time segment check cannot be determined without the method and reference value recorded as undecided in OP-SYS-001.
findings.requested_change: Define the failure criterion once the run-time check method and reference value are decided.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 and the requirement do not resolve whether the latch applies at the third fault or after the third reset. OP-SYS-002 records the ambiguity.
findings.requested_change: Specify the fault and reset sequence that causes the latch once the source owner decides it.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 permits a task name, CODE or CONFIG as the entity but does not define the entity for watchdog-reset fault code 8. OP-SYS-003 records the missing decision.
findings.requested_change: Specify the report entity for fault code 8 once the source owner decides it.

findings.description: The response contains <state>, but neither the requirement nor CON-SUP-113 defines its permitted values or meanings. OP-SYS-005 records the missing vocabulary.
findings.requested_change: Define the state values and their meanings once the source owner decides them.

findings.description: The trigger calls for detection when execution has not completed at the limit while the same requirement permits completion at that instant. CON-SUP-103 specifies both an execution longer than the limit and detection at expiry; OP-SYS-008 records the unresolved boundary and detection instant.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the equality boundary and detection instant with the source owner, then state a consistent trigger.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 supplies the CRC polynomial but not the remaining parameters and data-range details needed to reproduce the expected value. OP-SYS-010 records these missing details.
findings.requested_change: Specify the complete CRC definition and covered data once the source owner decides them.

findings.description: The requirement calls for eight reports for every GET FAULTS request, including when fewer exist; SYS-SUP-048 establishes an empty history after power restoration. OP-SYS-011 records that CON-SUP-113 does not define the response for fewer than eight reports.
findings.requested_change: Specify the response for zero through seven retained reports and qualify the eight-report case once the source owner decides the protocol.

findings.description: The requirement gives no deadline or precise event for driving the status signal high when its conditions hold. OP-SYS-012 records the missing timing decision.
findings.requested_change: Specify a measurable response time or event once the source owner decides it.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the reset cause to be readable by the service tool. SYS-SUP-032 transmits it at start-up, but the set defines no service request or response that retrieves it; OP-SYS-004 acknowledges the gap.
findings.requested_change: Define a service-tool mechanism for reading the reset cause once the source owner decides the interface.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-033 detects watchdog-reset fault code 8, but SYS-SUP-022 through SYS-SUP-024 exclude it from the safe-state and recovery responses. OP-SYS-007 records that the required reaction is undecided.
findings.requested_change: Resolve and specify the safe-state and recovery behavior for a watchdog-reset fault.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-046 requires retained fault history and SYS-SUP-038 requires reports from it, but the set does not require detected fault reports to be added to that history. Retention alone does not establish what the service tool can retrieve.
findings.requested_change: Specify when detected fault reports are recorded in the history and how the most recent reports are retained.

findings.description: CON-SUP-101 specifies three tasks released in order every 10 ms and T_DIAG released after T_OUT every tenth cycle. SYS-SUP-007 takes periods and checkpoint order from configuration, but the set does not specify these release periods and order as the required configuration or system behavior.
findings.requested_change: Specify the task release periods and order required by CON-SUP-101, including the T_DIAG relationship.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 does not define the program-code integrity method or the reference value against which the result is judged, so the check cannot be reproduced.
findings.requested_change: Define the integrity method and reference value for the start-up program-code check.

findings.description: A failed start-up program-code check cannot be determined until its method and reference value are defined.
findings.requested_change: Define how failure of the start-up program-code integrity check is determined.

findings.description: The requirement specifies segment size and frequency but does not define how the segment is checked or judged intact.
findings.requested_change: Define the run-time segment-check method and its reference value.

findings.description: Failure of a run-time program-code segment check cannot be determined until the check method and reference value are defined.
findings.requested_change: Define how failure of the run-time segment check is determined.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 and SYS-SUP-026 do not resolve whether the latch applies at the third fault or after the third supervisor reset.
findings.requested_change: Specify the fault and reset sequence that triggers the latch.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 permits a task name, CODE or CONFIG as the report entity but does not define the entity for watchdog-reset fault code 8.
findings.requested_change: Define the entity reported for watchdog-reset fault code 8.

findings.description: Neither SYS-SUP-037 nor CON-SUP-113 defines the permitted values and meanings of the returned state field.
findings.requested_change: Define the supervision states and their representations in the status response.

findings.description: The trigger detects an unfinished execution at the limit while the same requirement permits completion at that instant. CON-SUP-103 calls an execution longer than the limit an overrun and also specifies detection at expiry.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the completion boundary and detection instant, then make the trigger and permitted boundary consistent.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 supplies the CRC polynomial but not the remaining parameters and data-range details needed to reproduce the expected configuration CRC.
findings.requested_change: Define the complete CRC variant, covered data range and stored reference representation.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-038 requires eight reports for every GET FAULTS request, including when fewer exist; SYS-SUP-048 establishes an empty history after power restoration. CON-SUP-113 does not define that response.
findings.requested_change: Define the response for zero through seven retained reports and reconcile the requirement with that response.

findings.description: The requirement gives no deadline or precise event for driving the status signal high when its conditions hold.
findings.requested_change: Specify a verifiable event or maximum response time for driving the status signal high.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the reset cause to be readable by the service tool. SYS-SUP-032 transmits it at start-up, but the set defines no service request or response that retrieves it.
findings.requested_change: Define the service-tool mechanism for reading the reset cause and add the corresponding requirements.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-033 detects watchdog-reset fault code 8, but SYS-SUP-022 through SYS-SUP-024 exclude it from the specified safe-state and recovery responses.
findings.requested_change: Resolve and specify the safe-state and recovery response to a detected watchdog-reset fault.

findings.description: CON-SUP-115 requires a start-up configuration fault to latch the safe state. SYS-SUP-009 requires remaining safe until a power-on reset but does not require setting the latch retained across software and watchdog resets by SYS-SUP-028.
findings.requested_change: Specify that a start-up configuration fault sets the safe-state latch with the retention and clearing behavior required by CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-115.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires reset causes to be classified from reset flags. SYS-SUP-031 specifies the classifications but does not require use of the reset flags.
findings.requested_change: Include the required reset-flag basis for reset-cause classification.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-049 requires adding detected fault reports to retained history but specifies no ordering relative to the reset requested by SYS-SUP-024. A reset can therefore occur before the new report is retained, leaving SYS-SUP-038 without that report.
findings.requested_change: Specify when a detected fault report must be committed to retained history relative to recovery reset.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 and SYS-SUP-014 do not define the program-code integrity method or reference value, so the check cannot be reproduced.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the program-code integrity method and reference value.

findings.description: Failure of the start-up program-code check cannot be determined until its method and reference value are defined.
findings.requested_change: Define the check and its failure criterion after the program-code integrity decision is made.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-018 specifies segment size and frequency but not how a segment is checked or judged intact.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the run-time segment-check method and reference value.

findings.description: Failure of a run-time program-code segment check cannot be determined until the check method and reference value are defined.
findings.requested_change: Define the run-time check and its failure criterion after the program-code integrity decision is made.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 and SYS-SUP-026 do not resolve whether the latch applies at the third fault or after the third supervisor reset.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the precise event that triggers the latch.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 permits a task name, CODE or CONFIG as the report entity but does not define the entity for watchdog-reset fault code 8.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the entity value for a watchdog-reset fault report.

findings.description: Neither SYS-SUP-037 nor CON-SUP-113 defines the permitted values and meanings of the returned state field.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the state values and their meanings.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-004 detects an unfinished execution at the limit while also permitting completion at that instant. CON-SUP-103 calls an execution longer than the limit an overrun and specifies detection at expiry.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the equality boundary and detection instant, then make the trigger and permitted completion consistent.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 supplies the CRC polynomial but not the remaining parameters and data-range details needed to reproduce the configuration CRC.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the complete CRC parameters, covered data range and stored-value representation.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-038 requires eight reports for every GET FAULTS request, including when fewer exist; SYS-SUP-048 establishes an empty history after power restoration. CON-SUP-113 does not define that response.
findings.requested_change: Specify the eight-report case with its applicable condition and obtain the response for zero through seven retained reports.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-030 gives no deadline or precise event for driving the status signal high when its conditions hold.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify a verifiable response time or precise event for driving the signal high.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the reset cause to be readable by the service tool. SYS-SUP-032 transmits it at start-up, but the set defines no service request or response that retrieves it.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify how the service tool retrieves the reset cause.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-033 detects watchdog-reset fault code 8, but SYS-SUP-022 through SYS-SUP-024 exclude it from the specified safe-state and recovery responses.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the safe-state and recovery behavior for watchdog-reset faults.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 requires the fault report to be transmitted after entering the safe state. SYS-SUP-024 requires only that transmission complete before the reset request, so it permits the report to be transmitted before safe-state entry.
findings.requested_change: Specify the required ordering between safe-state entry and fault-report transmission, consistent with the report deadline.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 and SYS-SUP-014 do not define the program-code integrity method or reference value, so the check cannot be reproduced.
findings.requested_change: Define the program-code integrity method and reference value once the source decision is available.

findings.description: Failure of the start-up program-code check cannot be determined until its method and reference value are defined.
findings.requested_change: Define the conditions that constitute failure using the agreed integrity method and reference value.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-018 specifies segment size and frequency but not how a segment is checked or judged intact.
findings.requested_change: Define the run-time segment-check method and reference value once decided.

findings.description: Failure of a run-time program-code segment check cannot be determined until the check method and reference value are defined.
findings.requested_change: Define the conditions that constitute a failed segment check using the agreed method and reference value.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 and SYS-SUP-026 do not resolve whether the latch applies at the third fault or after the third supervisor reset.
findings.requested_change: Clarify the event that triggers the latch after the source owner resolves the sequence.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 permits a task name, CODE or CONFIG as the report entity but does not define the entity for watchdog-reset fault code 8.
findings.requested_change: Specify the entity for watchdog-reset reports after the source owner decides it.

findings.description: Neither SYS-SUP-037 nor CON-SUP-113 defines the permitted values and meanings of the returned state field.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify the permitted state values and their meanings.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-004 requires detection when execution has not completed at the limit while permitting completion at that instant. CON-SUP-103 calls an execution longer than the limit an overrun and specifies detection at expiry.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the equality boundary and detection instant with the source owner, then express a consistent rule.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 supplies the CRC polynomial but not the remaining parameters and data-range details needed to reproduce the configuration CRC.
findings.requested_change: Specify the complete CRC parameters, covered data and stored reference representation after the source decision.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-038 requires eight reports for every GET FAULTS request, including when fewer exist; SYS-SUP-048 establishes an empty history after power restoration. CON-SUP-113 does not define that response.
findings.requested_change: Limit the eight-report obligation to the applicable case and obtain and specify the response when fewer reports exist.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-030 gives no deadline or precise event for driving the status signal high when its conditions hold.
findings.requested_change: Specify a verifiable timing bound or event after the source owner decides it.

findings.description: CON-SUP-111 requires the reset cause to be readable by the service tool. SYS-SUP-032 transmits it at start-up, but the set defines no service request or response that retrieves it.
findings.requested_change: Obtain and specify a service-tool mechanism for reading the reset cause.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-033 detects watchdog-reset fault code 8, but SYS-SUP-022 through SYS-SUP-024 exclude it from the specified safe-state and recovery responses.
findings.requested_change: Resolve and specify the safe-state and recovery behavior for a detected watchdog-reset fault.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 requires transmission of the fault report after safe-state entry. SYS-SUP-024 imposes that ordering as part of the reset obligation but exempts latched safe states and start-up configuration faults; SYS-SUP-035 permits their reports before safe-state entry.
findings.requested_change: Specify the required report ordering for all applicable faults, including faults that latch the safe state.
